newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP to scale back Ok Tedi if no rain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP to scale back Ok Tedi if no rain.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would further scale back operations at the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea unless there was significant rain before week's end.

"If there is no significant rain before week's end, Ok Tedi Mining Ltd will further scale back mining operations to preserve sufficient fuel to maintain basic community services through a prolonged dry," BHP said.
Milling operations have already ceased and a broad range of secondary measures taken to reduce pressure on supplies, the company said.
The mine, located in PNG's Western Province, was forced about a week ago to shut the second of two semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mills after reviewing supplies of diesel fuel.
The mine's other SAG mill was shut the preceding week.
Rainfall this month so far had been only 62 mm, which is 378 mm down on the driest month since 1970, the company said.

BHP this week said it was maintaining open communications with customers who buy the mine's estimated 60,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a month since low water levels on the Fly River forced the suspension of barge transport of the concentrates,

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
